title: Smoked Jerk Chicken Leg Quarters
cook: 1½–2 hr, plus 5 min on the grill

items: 4 chicken leg quarters (about 3 lb total), fully thawed
2 Scotch bonnet or habanero peppers, stemmed and seeded
1 Tbsp fresh thyme leaves (or 1 tsp dried)

steps: Put the green onions, peppers, garlic, ginger, thyme, allspice, cinnamon, nutmeg, soy sauce, lime juice, brown sugar, oil, salt and black pepper in a blender and blend until mostly smooth. Set aside 3 Tbsp in the fridge for brushing at the end. Wear gloves when handling the peppers.

Cut 2–3 slashes down to the bone across each thigh and drumstick. Put the chicken in a gallon zip-top bag with the rest of the marinade, massage it into the cuts, seal and refrigerate 12–24 hr (at least 4 hr).
Bring the smoker to 275°F with apple or cherry wood. Run it hotter than you would for ribs, since chicken skin stays rubbery at 225°F.
Lift the chicken from the bag, let the excess marinade drip off, and set it skin side up on the grate. Throw out the used marinade. Smoke 1½–2 hr, until the thickest thigh reads 175–180°F.
Near the end, heat a grill to high, 450–500°F. Move the chicken to the grill skin side down and cook 2–3 min, then flip and cook 1–2 min, until the skin is crisp and charred in spots.
Brush the chicken with the reserved marinade, rest 5 min, and serve with the lime wedges.
tips: Heat level: 2 seeded Scotch bonnets is medium-hot. Leave the seeds in for hot, or use 1 pepper for medium.
No grill going? Broil skin side up about 6 inches from the heat 3–4 min instead. No smoker? Grill over indirect heat at 350°F for 45–60 min to the same temperature, then crisp over direct heat.
Leftover meat works in the Jerk Chicken Pizza with Mango Salsa in place of the seared breast.
storage: Fridge up to 4 days. Freezer up to 3 months. Reheat in a 375°F oven 15–20 min, until it reaches 165°F.
